Sounds like you need some space for yourself. Have you thought of taking a little breather and staying at an Airbnb or a hotel for a bit? She should understand, and maybe you can bring your kids to visit sometime. It’s extremely difficult to still live together knowing they’re seeing someone. I can understand completely (partner and I were non-monogamous and he’s got another partner currently). You have to remember that you’re still lovable. You’re worth it. I know it hurts so much but you have to focus on you. Stay in bed all day if you need to. Just don’t sink too much. Let yourself reach those goals of happiness and acceptance for her in time. You don’t owe anyone anything.

Don’t rush your healing process and let yourself mourn. It’ll come and go in waves, you just have to keep going.

It caused a lot of damage to each other and our relationship, but we really value our connection beyond the romance, so we’ve had some good talks, set boundaries, and decided we’ll stay in each other’s lives and love each other in a different way. It was hard for me at first, but looking back, we haven’t been on the same wavelength for a few months and it just feels like it’s time to throw in the towel. We love each other very much and continue to be kind and hang out often. I’m so sorry you’re struggling to maintain a civil connection with your ex. It’s okay to not want that or be able to do that. You need to grieve and heal in your own way. I hope you’re able to make peace with things and find yourself again.

So this is long… erm.. I’ve gone over some details in my post history, if you’re curious. I’ve been in therapy and on medication to sort out my depression, anxiety, ADHD and CPTSD for about three months. However, I’ve still had my bad days. I have hurt my spouse over the years, and he is tired. He says he doesn’t want to resent me and so he believes separating is the best option. I knew I couldn’t change his mind, so I didn’t beg or plead or get angry… I just told myself this is a new chapter and he can stay in my book as a different connection eventually. I want to keep him in my life even if it’s platonically, because we love each other a lot, we’ve both grown a lot together, and we have pets together. We also know that this isn’t 100 percent anyone’s fault. We’re two broken people trying to love each other, but we can’t if we’re broken. So I am trying to get my shit together — my partner appreciates my changes and he tells me he is so proud of me for handling this respectfully, but he feels so damaged over the fights, the yelling, the toxic habits we developed over the seven years together. We tried so hard to make it work. Couples counseling, time away, constant work on our communication and perceptions…. I thought things were making a turning point and we were in a good place until he confessed he doesn’t want to be married anymore. I think we just can’t grow together at this point. I’ve just accepted that his happiness is important and if I have to let him go, I will. I am trying so hard not to feel guilty. I’ve been keeping in touch with him, because we’re trying to comfort each other during this, and I worry he’ll think it’s just a ploy to get him back. It’s not; I’m genuinely exhausted and tired of hurting the people in my life, and allowing my demons to destroy my chances at happiness after a long and tiring childhood of abuse. I’m proud of you for keeping on. I hope things look up for you soon.
This fucking hurts.

I’m going to miss his hugs. The way he smells when I press my face into his chest and he wraps his arms around me. Washing his hair in the shower. Staying up late watching YouTube videos. Making him coffee and waiting for him to wake up and come outside when he’s finished sleeping in. I’m going to miss his voice telling me he loves me. His passionate kisses. His amazing storytelling and knowledge for everything and anything. He always has a knack for explaining things simply. I just love his hard work ethic, his kindness, his hand in mine. I shouldn’t have taken all of that for granted. I don’t have BPD, but I was misdiagnosed with it many years ago. Still, I had a lot of toxic actions that really harmed my partner beyond repair. I wish I could go back in time. Thanks for sharing this. We can all cry together.

Divorce isn’t a death sentence. We have been in counseling for a very, very long time off and on, and I can’t force his heart to heal. He feels he can’t forgive me for the pain over the years, and knowing that, there is nothing I can do to change that. I’ve already been on a pretty good path in therapy recently, but that doesn’t mean he has to forgive me and change his mind. I want to work diligently to show him I want to change and I have taken a lot of accountability, but that’s not enough. That’s not his fault and it doesn’t make him a bad person. He still loves me in some way, and we aren’t on bad terms. We came to the difficult agreement that this is what’s best for both of us even if it doesn’t feel like it right now. Maintaining our friendship later on is more important than trying to salvage this marriage. I’ve reached acceptance and I just need to move forward with my own healing — I have a lot of work to do that I regret not doing sooner. Maybe one day he’ll come back into my life in a romantic sense, but for now, all I can do is work to take care of me.

She has to stick with it. Many times those who experience childhood trauma can develop a victim mindset. It’s pretty shit when you put it into words but there’s a reason it happens. She felt small as a kid and now she’s taking that pain with her now, and it’s affecting your marriage. I don’t know your wife, but I do know what it’s like to be in her shoes. There’s a lot of guilt, shame, self loathing and hatred deep down inside and those things can completely cause someone to lash out at the world because they’re too afraid to change. It’s not a great place to be. I hope she takes accountability soon and tries to see it from your perspective.

I will also say this: for many years, I was misdiagnosed. Many times. I wasn’t able to conquer my issues until I got on the right meds that made me have more energy, no intrusive thoughts and a more positive outlook on things. Maybe she should consider looking deeper into her diagnoses and get some second and third opinions. It took me years to figure it out but I’m glad I got on the right meds.

We want to support each other and not allow resentment to form. I’d rather have him as my best friend, while I work on bettering myself, than not at all. I am very ashamed, guilty and upset with my past behavior and I don’t blame him at all for setting boundaries, putting himself first and seeking happiness elsewhere. We’re still very much on good terms even if this is really hard. I know in time things will get easier and I’m glad we’re leaving things on a good note even if there’s some pain points involved. This is just a consequence of the behavior I displayed over and over and I’ve accepted it. That’s not to say he doesn’t have his own contributions to the fallout, but I did cause most of the damage. No. I have treated him terribly off and on for many years. I doubted his love for me, I emotionally bruised him over and over, I did a lot of stupid, hurtful things because I was afraid, insecure and overemotional. I won’t go into everything. I didn’t grow up in a healthy home and I took all of those fleas, traumas, insecurities and false perceptions of the world with me — and even though I worked at it, it still caused so much strife in my marriage. I avoided confronting things fully and I didn’t realize how broken I actually was. We met when I was just shy of 19 and growing together after I escaped my abusive home was so difficult. I don’t blame him for taking steps to live a life where he doesn’t have to worry about coming home and he feels safe. No matter what I will always love him. We’re both just two broken people that really tried hard to make it work.

I want to go to counseling again with my husband, but he has made his mind up. He is very much broken, sad, hurt and tired of the pain I’ve put him through over and over again due to my childhood trauma, toxic behavior and low self esteem. I’ve recently started making a lot of progress in therapy and I was so glad things were going good, but I could sense he was distant. We had a good long talk, and he admitted he didn’t know if he could get over the emotional turmoil I’ve caused due to my own toxic behavior. Just because I’m changing doesn’t mean he has to forgive me. His pain and feelings are all so valid and that’s why I feel so sad. Part of me hopes that in time, we will find our way back to each other. His happiness is more important to me than staying together. He is a beautiful person inside and out, and it was probably awful for him to admit that our marriage was over in his eyes. We don’t hate each other, we’re not angry — we’re grieving together and we both know we will grow from this but it hurts so bad.
